description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake loaded with fresh seafood and crisp green onions, pan-fried to a golden perfection. Its satisfyingly chewy interior and crispy edges make it an irresistible appetizer or light meal, often enjoyed with a tangy dipping sauce. This traditional dish offers a delightful blend of oceanic flavors and aromatic vegetables, creating a truly authentic Korean culinary experience.

about 10-12 stalks, cut into 3-4 inch lengths

instructions.title: Prepare the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, cold water, beaten egg, and salt until just combined. A few lumps are okay. Do not overmix the batter, as this can make the pancake tough. Set the batter aside to rest for 10-15 minutes while you prepare other ingredients.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse and pat dry all assorted seafood. If using larger pieces, cut them into bite-sized portions. Prepare the green onions by washing them and cutting them into approximately 3-4 inch long pieces. Thinly slice the onion and red chili if using. Keep seafood and vegetables separate for now.

instructions.title: Make the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, gochugaru (if using), and sesame seeds. Stir well to mix all the ingredients. Taste and adjust seasonings if necessary. Set aside; this sauce will be served alongside your freshly made pancakes.

instructions.title: Assemble and Cook the First Pancake
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring it coats the bottom evenly. Pour about 1/4 of the batter into the hot pan, spreading it slightly to form a thin, round pancake. Immediately arrange 1/4 of the prepared seafood, green onions, and sliced onion evenly over the batter.

instructions.title: Achieve Golden Crispiness
instructions.text: Cook the pancake for about 5-7 minutes on one side, or until the edges are golden brown and crispy and the batter is mostly set. Gently press down on the pancake with a spatula to ensure even contact with the pan and to encourage crispiness. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges if needed to enhance browning.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Cook the second side for another 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and the seafood is fully cooked through. If using red chili, you can place a few slices on top for garnish after flipping. Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Cut the large pancake into wedges or squares. Repeat the cooking process with the remaining batter and ingredients to make additional pancakes. Serve the warm Haemul Pajeon immediately with the prepared dipping sauce on the side. Enjoy this crispy, savory Korean delight!

tips: Use very cold water for the batter to help achieve a super crispy texture for your pancake.
Do not overcrowd the pan; cook one pancake at a time to ensure even browning and crispiness.
Press down gently on the pancake with a spatula while cooking to maximize surface contact and create a flatter, crispier result.
article:
Craving a culinary adventure that tantalizes your taste buds with fresh seafood and savory goodness? Look no further than Haemul Pajeon, the iconic Korean seafood pancake. This beloved dish is a staple in Korean cuisine, celebrated for its crispy edges, soft interior, and generous medley of ocean treasures and vibrant green onions. Whether you’re a seasoned Korean food enthusiast or new to its delights, learning about and making Haemul Pajeon promises a delicious and rewarding experience. It’s perfect as an appetizer, a satisfying snack, or even a light meal, especially when paired with a traditional Korean rice wine on a rainy day.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon (해물파전) literally translates to "seafood green onion pancake." At its heart, it's a savory pancake made from a simple flour-based batter, generously studded with various seafood and, crucially, an abundance of green onions. Unlike thinner, crepe-like pancakes, Haemul Pajeon is typically thicker, boasting a delightful contrast between its golden-brown, crispy exterior and its tender, flavorful inside. The green onions aren't just a garnish; they form the backbone of the pancake, providing a fresh, slightly pungent flavor and a satisfying texture. The seafood, often a mix of shrimp, squid, and mussels, infuses the entire dish with a rich umami depth that is simply irresistible. This dish is more than just food; it's a comfort food often enjoyed communally, embodying the warmth and generosity of Korean hospitality.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon

Creating an authentic Haemul Pajeon requires fresh ingredients and a few pantry staples. Here’s what you’ll need:

For the Pancake Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour (or Korean pancake mix, buchim garu, for extra crispiness)
*   1/4 cup glutinous rice flour (optional, for added chewiness and crispness)
*   1 large egg
*   1.5 cups cold water or anchovy broth (for deeper flavor)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1/4 teaspoon baking powder (optional, for a lighter texture)

For the Filling:
*   2 cups green onions, cut into 3-4 inch lengths (the white and light green parts are best)
*   1 cup mixed seafood (e.g., shrimp, squid rings, mussels, oysters), cleaned and chopped into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced (optional)
*   1-2 red or green chili peppers, thinly sliced (optional, for heat and color)
*   Vegetable oil, for frying

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sugar
*   1/2 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1/2 teaspoon minced garlic
*   1/4 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1 tablespoon chopped green onion (from the dark green parts)

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon: Step-by-Step Guide

Follow these steps to create your own delicious Haemul Pajeon:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** Thoroughly clean all seafood. For squid, remove the clear quill and skin, then slice into rings or bite-sized pieces. Peel and devein shrimp. If using mussels, scrub them clean. Pat all seafood dry. Cut the green onions into roughly 3-4 inch segments. Slice the optional onion and chili peppers.

2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, glutinous rice flour (if using), salt, and baking powder (if using). In a separate bowl, lightly beat the egg, then add the cold water or broth. Gradually pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, whisking until just combined. A few lumps are okay; avoid overmixing, as this can lead to a tough pancake. The batter should have a consistency similar to thin pancake batter.

3.  **Combine Ingredients (Optional Method):** Some prefer to mix all ingredients (seafood, green onions, optional onion/chili) directly into the batter. However, for a more aesthetically pleasing and traditional Haemul Pajeon, you can layer them in the pan.

4.  **Cook the Pancake:** Heat a large, non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring it coats the bottom of the pan evenly. Once the oil is shimmering, arrange about half of your green onion segments in a single layer on the pan.

5.  **Pour and Arrange:** Ladle about 1 cup of batter over the green onions, spreading it gently to form a round pancake. Quickly arrange a portion of your mixed seafood and any remaining green onions, sliced onion, and chili peppers on top of the wet batter. Press them down gently so they adhere.

6.  **Fry until Golden:** Cook for 5-7 minutes on the first side, or until the edges are golden brown and crispy, and the top begins to set. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges to help crisp them up.

7.  **Flip and Finish:** Carefully flip the pancake using a wide spatula (or two spatulas for larger pancakes). Cook for another 5-7 minutes on the second side, until golden brown, crispy, and cooked through. The seafood should be opaque and the green onions slightly charred.

8.  **Prepare the Dipping Sauce:** While the pancake cooks, combine all dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl and stir well.

9.  **Serve:** Transfer the Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice into wedges or squares and serve immediately with the dipping sauce. Repeat the cooking process for any remaining batter and ingredients.

## Tips for the Perfect Crispy Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that perfect balance of crispy exterior and tender interior for your Haemul Pajeon is key. Here are some pro tips:

*   **Hot Oil is Crucial:** Ensure your pan and oil are hot before adding the batter. This helps create an instant crisp crust.
*   **Don't Skimp on Oil:** A generous amount of oil is essential for frying, not just cooking. It contributes significantly to the crispiness.
*   **Thin Batter Layer:** While Haemul Pajeon is thicker than some pancakes, avoid making the batter layer too thick in the pan. A thinner layer promotes crispiness.
*   **Use Cold Water/Broth:** Cold liquid helps prevent gluten development, leading to a more tender and less chewy pancake.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pan:** Cook one Haemul Pajeon at a time, or at most two if your pan is very large, to maintain consistent heat and ensure even cooking.
*   **Green Onions are Key:** The sheer volume of green onions isn't just for flavor; they contribute to the pancake's structure and unique texture.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed hot and fresh, straight from the pan. Slice it into bite-sized wedges or squares for easy sharing. It’s traditionally paired with makgeolli, a lightly sparkling Korean rice wine, especially on a rainy day when the sound of sizzling pancakes is said to mimic raindrops. However, it also goes wonderfully with a cold beer or a shot of soju. Serve it alongside other Korean side dishes (banchan) like kimchi for a complete meal.

The dipping sauce described above is a classic accompaniment, offering a perfect balance of savory, tangy, and a hint of spice that cuts through the richness of the pancake. Feel free to adjust the sweetness or spice level to your preference.

## Variations and Ingredient Substitutions

One of the beautiful aspects of Haemul Pajeon is its versatility. Don't be afraid to experiment:

*   **Seafood Combinations:** While shrimp, squid, and mussels are common, feel free to use scallops, oysters, clams, or even imitation crab meat. A pre-packaged frozen seafood mix works well for convenience.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Beyond green onions, consider adding thinly sliced carrots, bell peppers, mushrooms (like shiitake or oyster mushrooms), or even a handful of chopped kimchi (though this would technically make it Kimchi Pajeon!).
*   **Batter Enhancements:** If you can find it, Korean pancake mix (buchim garu) is specifically formulated for crispiness and often contains seasoning. Adding a touch of rice flour to your regular flour mix will also enhance the crisp texture.
*   **Spice Level:** For a spicier kick, increase the amount of gochugaru in the dipping sauce or chop some fresh serrano or jalapeño peppers into the batter.
*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Option:** Omit the seafood and egg, replacing them with a larger variety of vegetables and perhaps some crumbled firm tofu or rehydrated shiitake mushrooms for an umami boost. Use a flax egg or commercial egg replacer for the binder.

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a Korean dish; it's an experience. Its delightful combination of textures and flavors, from the crispy exterior to the tender seafood and aromatic green onions, makes it a universally loved comfort food. Whether you follow this guide precisely or add your own creative twist, making this savory pancake is sure to bring a taste of Korea right into your kitchen. So, gather your ingredients, heat up your pan, and get ready to enjoy a truly unforgettable culinary treat!
